assertions.assertion: a receipt inherited from the commit is not evidence that this run derived the ledger
assertions.detail: expected the guard to exit 0 when no derivation ran in this run; got 0:

assertions.assertion: arm B is recorded as skipped, so the pass is explained rather than silent
assertions.detail: expected rederived_ledger_vs_working_tree.ran === false in the report; got {"ran":false,"pages_examined":0,"mismatched":0,"examples":[],"receipt":null}

assertions.assertion: the run still examined pages, so exiting 0 is not exiting 0 having done nothing (Rule 0)
a page rewritten after an in-run derivation is still a hard failure
assertions.detail: expected the guard to exit non-zero; got 1. Arm B has been weakened.

assertions.assertion: the failure is arm B naming the stale page, not some unrelated error
assertions.detail: expected arm B to have run and found a mismatch; got {"ran":true,"pages_examined":2,"mismatched":1,"examples":[{"file":"alpha/index.html","ledger":"6e2317529b74ada5fbab48d2","disk":"3e0a07a69d93b639d31d709e"}]}

assertions.assertion: re-deriving a correct ledger leaves it byte-identical, which is what made the old proxy wrong
assertions.detail: expected an unchanged ledger from a no-op derivation; changed=false, exit=0

assertions.assertion: the no-op derivation still writes a receipt that differs from the committed one, so it is admitted as this run's
assertions.detail: the no-op derivation left the receipt byte-identical to the committed one, so it is now indistinguishable from an inherited receipt

assertions.assertion: a no-op in-run derivation over an intact tree passes with arm B having run
assertions.detail: expected exit 0 with arm B run over >0 pages; exit=0, armB={"ran":true,"pages_examined":2,"mismatched":0,"examples":[]}

assertions.assertion: ledgerDerivationReceipt compares the receipt on disk against the one committed at HEAD
assertions.detail: the HEAD comparison is gone from scripts/lib/sitemap_ledger.mjs; a committed receipt would again pass as this run's

assertions.assertion: the derivation receipt is not tracked in this repository
assertions.detail: artifacts/validation/lastmod-derivation-receipt.json is tracked at HEAD. It is evidence about one run; committing it is what made every later checkout start with a receipt it had not written (93977956f).

assertions.assertion: the derivation receipt is covered by .gitignore, so `git add -A` cannot reintroduce it
assertions.detail: artifacts/validation/lastmod-derivation-receipt.json is not matched by .gitignore, so the next bot release commit re-commits it and the daily failure returns.

assertions.assertion: the commit helper does not stage with a bare `git add -A`
assertions.detail: the commit helper stages with `git add -A -- . ':(exclude)artifacts/validation/*receipt*.json'`, which sweeps every per-run artifact into a main commit

assertions.assertion: the staging command still stages the content a release publishes
assertions.detail: expected published-page.html to be staged; staged=["artifacts/validation/workflow-yaml-inventory.json","published-page.html"] exit=0. A staging rule that drops published content would make the lane exit 0 having published nothing.

assertions.assertion: the staging command still stages validation artifacts that later runs consume
assertions.detail: workflow-yaml-inventory.json is read with no fallback by validate_workflow_artifacts.mjs and validate_workflow_runtime_mutations.mjs; excluding artifacts/validation wholesale freezes an input. staged=["artifacts/validation/workflow-yaml-inventory.json","published-page.html"]

assertions.assertion: the staging command refuses to stage the per-run derivation receipt
